title: Breakthrough
summary: Giving up one or two pawns to create a passed pawn, after counting whether the enemy king gets there in time.
part.classic.title: The classic breakthrough
part.classic.summary: Three pawns against three: the middle pawn is sacrificed, then its neighbour, and the third one queens.
part.count.title: Count before you sacrifice
part.count.summary: Pawns you give away don't come back. Before the first one, check whether the enemy king catches the new passer.
part.side.title: Far from the king
part.side.summary: The passed pawn has to be born on the side where the enemy king isn't.
part.kingside.title: When the king attacks the pawns
part.kingside.summary: The same blow on the kingside, as on Wikipedia: the black king threatens the pawns, and the breakthrough comes first.
part.defense.title: The defence
part.defense.summary: The defender to move pushes the middle pawn. Then he recaptures with the right pawn.
part.finish.title: Summary
part.finish.summary: Three rules for your games, the blow once more and a game against the machine.
step.t_classic: White to move. Three pawns against three, face to face, and both kings far away. No pawn is passed, and the black king can't help. Can White get a pawn to the eighth rank?
step.t_classic.hint1: One pawn alone can't get past three. But if you give away one or two pawns, the black pawns must capture and step out of the way.
step.t_classic.hint2: Start with the middle pawn. What does Black do if it advances and threatens to take on a7 or c7?
step.classicWhy: The move is b6! It threatens bxa7 or bxc7 and queening, so Black has to capture. If he takes with the a-pawn, I play c6!: after bxc6, the a5-pawn walks freely to a8. If he takes with the c-pawn, I play a6!: after bxa6, the c5-pawn gets through. If he doesn't take, my b6-pawn takes on a7 or c7 and queens. That's eight pieces, more than the endgame tablebase stores, so I checked it with the engine: only b6 wins here. Starting with a6 or c6 achieves nothing, and neither does waiting with the king.
step.d_classic: Black took with the a-pawn. Watch the second sacrifice.
step.d_classic.m1: c6! Another pawn given away, on purpose. It threatens cxb7.
step.d_classic.m2: Black takes. Notice: the b7-pawn has left, and it was the one guarding a6.
step.d_classic.m3: a6. No black pawn can touch this pawn. Two moves to go.
step.d_classic.m4: The black king runs, but it's much too far.
step.d_classic.m6: The black king is still far from a8.
step.d_classic.m7: Queen. Two pawns given, one new queen. The black pawns on b6 and c6 are a long way from the first rank.
step.otherCapture: And if Black takes with the c-pawn? It's the mirror image. Now the c-file has no black pawn in front of my c5-pawn, and only the b7-pawn guards c6. The second sacrifice is a6!, to deflect that pawn. The rule: after the first sacrifice, look at which file became free; that file's pawn will get through, and the other one sacrifices itself to remove the guard.
step.classicMove: Your turn. Black took with the c-pawn. White to move and win.
step.classicMove.hint: The c-file is free in front of your c5-pawn. Who guards c6? Deflect that pawn.
step.classicMove.done: That's it. a6 deflected the b7-pawn, and the c-pawn went straight through. Only that path won.
step.t_count: Same idea, but now the black king is on e8, closer. White has already played b6 and Black took with the a-pawn. Does the breakthrough still work? Count before you play.
step.t_count.hint1: Play the breakthrough in your head to the end: c6, bxc6, a6. Now it's Black's move. Where must the king get to in order to stop the a6-pawn?
step.t_count.hint2: The a6-pawn queens in two moves. The black king has to reach b7 first. Count the king's moves from e8, remembering that c7 is taken by a black pawn.
step.square: The count is the rule of the square. After c6, bxc6 and a6, the pawn is two squares from queening, and Black is to move. The king on e8 needs three moves to reach b7: d8, c8, b7. The pawn needs two. The king is too late, and the breakthrough works.
step.tooClose: Now the black king is on d8, one square closer. After c6, bxc6 and a6, the king goes to c8 and then b7, and catches the pawn. Here the breakthrough fails, and whoever gave the pawns away is left with nothing. That's why the count comes before the first sacrifice: a pawn given is a pawn gone.
step.countMove: Back to the king on e8. White to move and win. Make the breakthrough and take the pawn to the seventh rank.
step.countMove.hint: You've already counted: the king on e8 arrives late. Deflect the b7-pawn and run with the a-pawn.
step.countMove.done: That's it. The black king went to d7, but the pawn is already on a7 and queens next move.
step.t_side: White to move. Different pawns: White on c5 and e5, Black on d7, e7 and d6. The black king is on h8. There's a breakthrough here. With which pawn?
step.t_side.hint1: Try both advances, c6 and e6. After each one, a black pawn captures. Which white pawn is left with a free file?
step.t_side.hint2: One of the advances leaves the e5-pawn still blocked by the e7-pawn. The other frees a pawn on a file far from the black king.
step.sideWhy: e6! It threatens exd7 and queening. If the d7-pawn takes, the c5-pawn has nobody in front or beside it: c6, c7, c8. And the black king on h8 is on the other side of the board. c6 is no use: the e5-pawn would still be blocked by the e7-pawn. One more thing: with the black king on a8, close to the c-file, this same e6 would not win. The passed pawn has to be born far from the king.
step.d_side: Now the mirror: black pawns on c7, d7 and d6, and the black king on a8. The breakthrough is on the other side, so the new pawn is born far from the king.
step.d_side.m1: c6! It threatens cxd7 and queening on d8.
step.d_side.m2: Black takes. The e-file is now free in front of my pawn.
step.d_side.m3: e6. Nobody can touch this pawn.
step.d_side.m4: The black king comes, but it's too far.
step.d_side.m6: The king wanted to reach d7. Too late.
step.sideMove: Back to the king on h8. White to move and win.
step.sideMove.hint: Advance the pawn that forces the d7-pawn to capture and frees the pawn on the file far from the king.
step.sideMove.done: That's it. e6 pulled the d7-pawn out of the way, and the c-pawn went alone to c7. The black king never came close.
step.t_wiki: White to move. Now it's on the kingside, and the black king is on g3, right next to the white pawns. It threatens to go to g4 and attack the pawns. What does White play?
step.t_wiki.hint1: Waiting doesn't help: the black king will attack the pawns. Look for a move that creates a passed pawn by force.
step.t_wiki.hint2: It's the same idea as in the first part, with the middle pawn of this wing.
step.wikiWhy: g6! It's the b6 of the first part, now on the kingside. If fxg6, then h6! and, after gxh6, the f5-pawn gets through. If hxg6, then f6! and, after gxf6, the h5-pawn gets through. Wikipedia uses this example in its article on the passed pawn. It's eight pieces, so I checked it with the engine: only g6 wins. The black king on g3 is close to the white pawns, but far from the eighth rank, which is where the new pawn is going.
step.d_wiki: Black took with the h-pawn. Watch the second sacrifice.
step.d_wiki.m1: f6! Another pawn given, to deflect the g7-pawn.
step.d_wiki.m2: The g7-pawn takes. Now nobody guards h6.
step.d_wiki.m3: h6. Nothing stands between this pawn and h8.
step.d_wiki.m4: The black king comes back, but it has a long way to go.
step.d_wiki.m6: The king got close, one move too late.
step.wikiMove: Your turn. Here Black took with the f-pawn. White to move and win.
step.wikiMove.hint: The f5-pawn has no black pawn in front of it. Who guards f6? Deflect that pawn with the other sacrifice.
step.wikiMove.done: That's it. h6 removed the g7-pawn, and the f-pawn ran. The black pawns that remain are far from the first rank.
step.t_defense: Same position, but now Black is to move. You are the defender. How do you stop the g6 breakthrough?
step.t_defense.hint1: If you let g6 happen, you've seen what comes. Look for a move that takes the sacrifice away from White.
step.t_defense.hint2: One of your pawns can advance and touch the white pawns. Of the three advances, only one works.
step.defenseWhy: ...g6! Now, if White captures, the pawns get exchanged and no white pawn gets through. The other advances lose: after ...f6 comes h6!, and after ...h6 comes f6!, each one opening the way for a pawn. That's what Wikipedia shows, and the engine agrees: only ...g6 holds. The idea works on either side of the board: the defender pushes the middle pawn into contact before the attacker does.
step.defenseMove: Black played ...g6, and White took with the h-pawn. Black to move and draw. Which pawn do you recapture with?
step.defenseMove.hint: Recapture with the pawn on the same side the white pawn came from. That way the other white pawn still has a black pawn in front of it.
step.defenseMove.done: That's it. After fxg6 and fxg6, one pawn each is left, blocked: a draw. Had you taken with the f-pawn, f6! would have given White a passed pawn.
step.sameSide: Now White took with the f-pawn. Same rule: recapture with the pawn on the side the white pawn came from, the f7-pawn. If you took with the h-pawn, h6! would open the way for the h5-pawn.
step.sameSideMove.hint: The white pawn came from f5. Recapture with your f-file pawn.
step.sameSideMove.done: That's it. The pawns get exchanged, and one pawn each is left, face to face. No white pawn gets through.
step.recap: Three rules for your games. First: with three pawns against three, face to face, the middle pawn is sacrificed first; then its neighbour removes the pawn that guards the file that became free. Second: before the first sacrifice, count whether the enemy king catches the new pawn; it has to be born far from that king. Third: the defender to move pushes the middle pawn into contact with the other side's pawns; when they capture, recapture with the pawn on the same side.
step.recapMove: The blow once more, before the game. Black took with the a-pawn. White to move and win.
step.recapMove.hint: The a5-pawn has a free file; only the b7-pawn guards a6.
step.recapMove.done: That's it. c6 deflected the b7-pawn, and the a5-pawn got through.
step.playIntro: Now a game against the machine. Black has already taken with the a-pawn, and the black king is on f1, far away. Only one move wins. Count, and play on until you have a queen.
step.finish: White to move and win. Good luck.
ex.e01: White to move and win. Two pawns against one, and the black king on d8.
ex.e01.hint: The a6-pawn is two squares from queening, but the a7-pawn is in the way. Get it out of the way.
ex.e01.solution: b6! If axb6, a7, and the king on d8 doesn't reach b7 in time. If Black doesn't take, for example with Kc8, bxa7 and the pawn queens. White's king moves only draw.
ex.e02: White to move and win. Black has already taken the first pawn with the a-pawn, and the black king is on f3.
ex.e02.hint: Which white pawn has no black pawn in front of it? Deflect the pawn that guards its next square.
ex.e02.solution: c6! After bxc6, the a5-pawn goes to a6, a7 and a8, and the king on f3 can't catch it. Only c6 wins.
ex.e03: White to move and win. This time the c-pawn did the capturing.
ex.e03.hint: The c-file is free. Who guards c6?
ex.e03.solution: a6! After bxa6, the c5-pawn runs: c6, c7, c8. If Black takes on c5 instead, axb7 and the pawn queens on b8. Only a6 wins.
ex.e04: White to move and win. The breakthrough is now on the kingside, and Black has already taken with the f-pawn.
ex.e04.hint: The f5-pawn has no black pawn in front of it. Who guards f6?
ex.e04.solution: h6! After gxh6, f6, and the f-pawn runs to f8. If Black doesn't take, hxg7 and the pawn queens on g8. Only h6 wins.
ex.e05: White to move and win. On the kingside, Black took with the h-pawn.
ex.e05.hint: Which white pawn has a free file? First deflect the guard, then run.
ex.e05.solution: f6! and, after gxf6, h6: the h-pawn runs to h8. The order matters: starting with h6 doesn't win.
ex.e06: White to move and win. White pawns on d5 and f5; black pawns on e7, f7 and e6. The black king is on h8.
ex.e06.hint: Which advance forces a black pawn to capture and frees a white pawn on a file far from the king?
ex.e06.solution: f6! After exf6, d6, and the d-pawn runs to d8, far from the king on h8. If Black doesn't take, the f6-pawn takes on e7 and queens. Exchanging on e6 only draws.
ex.e07: Black to move and draw. Black played ...b6 to stop the breakthrough, and White took with the a-pawn. Which pawn do you recapture with?
ex.e07.hint: For each recapture, check which white pawn would be left with no black pawn in front of it.
ex.e07.solution: ...axb6! After cxb6 and cxb6, one pawn each is left, face to face: a draw. If ...cxb6?, c6! and the c-pawn gets through.
ex.e08: White to move and win. Three pawns against two, but the black king is on c8, right next to the pawns.
ex.e08.hint: Count before you sacrifice: after a breakthrough, does the black king catch the new pawn? If it does, look for another plan.
ex.e08.solution: Here the breakthrough only draws: the king on c8 catches the new pawn. With an extra pawn, the plan is to bring the king. Any king move, such as Kf2, wins; a6, b6 or c6 right now throw the win away.
ex.e09: White to move and win. The black king is on b3, close to the pawns, but it's White's move.
ex.e09.hint: Which white pawn has a free file in front of it? Who guards its next square?
ex.e09.solution: a6! If bxa6, c6 and c7: the king on b3 is close, but it doesn't reach c8 in time. If bxc5, axb7 and the pawn queens on b8. Only a6 wins; the nearby king doesn't change the count, because the c-pawn is three moves from a queen.
ex.e10: Black to move and draw. Three white pawns against two, and the black king on d7. What do you do before White plays b6?
ex.e10.hint: Push a pawn into contact with the white pawns to take the breakthrough away, and let the king handle the rest.
ex.e10.solution: ...a6! After bxa6, the king goes to c8 and, after c6, to b8, in front of the a-pawn. The c7-pawn blocks the c6-pawn. Only ...a6 draws, and after that only Kc8 and Kb8 hold.
key.classic: Three pawns against three, kings far away: only b6 wins (checked with the engine). The structure appears in alexandra_botez's Lichess study "BREAKTHROUGH", with other king positions.
key.afterAxb6: After b6 axb6: only c6 wins (tablebase).
key.afterCxb6: After b6 cxb6: only a6 wins (tablebase).
key.count: The king on e8 is one move late: c6 still wins. With the king on d8, the breakthrough fails.
key.side: Only e6 wins: the c-pawn is born far from the king on h8. Own position.
key.wiki: The Wikipedia example (Passed pawn): the black king threatens the pawns, and only g6 wins (checked with the engine).
key.wikiDefense: The same position with Black to move: only ...g6 holds (Wikipedia; checked with the engine).
history: Breakthrough is the name for piercing the opponent's defence, often by means of a sacrifice; that is how Wikipedia's chess glossary defines the term, citing Seirawan and Silman. In pawn endings, the best-known form is three pawns against three, face to face: the middle pawn is sacrificed, then its neighbour, and the third one queens. Endgame manuals give the theme its own place: de la Villa has an ending called "Breakthroughs when the king is far" in 100 Endgames You Must Know, and Dvoretsky a section "Breakthrough" in his chapter on pawn endings. Wikipedia, in its article on the passed pawn, uses the kingside version, with the black king threatening the pawns, and shows the defence ...g6 when Black is to move. I could not find who first published the position.
practice: Final training: White pawns on c5 and e5, Black pawns on d7, e7 and d6, and the black king on h8. Find the breakthrough and take the pawn all the way to a queen.
